title: feat(types,plugin-designer)!: draw the data-model and process designers' read members; respell onDelete as deleteBehavior (objectui#11434, PR 2 of 3)
body:
Part of #11434

Clause-②: yes

PR 2 of at most 3 under the seat's ruling 5946170549 (staged option B, the "Read" section): the readers for the members the ruling settled READ on the **data-model** and **process** designers, and the `onDelete` respelling. PR 1 (objectui#11451, merged as `c4ab6d09a`) held every retirement. The page designer, the shared canvases and the report designer are PR 3, the last one, which carries the card's closing line. This PR leaves the card open on purpose.

After this PR, no member of `DataModelDesignerSchema` or `ProcessDesignerSchema`, or of the records they hold, stays declared and unread.

## What draws each member

"Read" means the renderer draws it. Each row is pinned by a render probe through the real `SchemaRenderer` and registry that compares the drawn markup with the member set and unset. The node members are compared with the node selected, because the property panel draws them. Each row also names WHAT is drawn, so a member drawn somewhere meaningless still fails. No pin relies on a style value alone.

| Member | Drawn as | Pin |
|---|---|---|
| `DataModelField.label` | muted text beside the field name | `DataModelDesigner.readers-11434.test.tsx` |
| `DataModelField.unique` | a `UQ` badge beside the `PK` one | same |
| `DataModelField.defaultValue` | `= VALUE` after the type, as JSON (a string quoted, `null` visible), and in the row tooltip | same |
| `DataModelField.description` | the row tooltip | same |
| `DataModelRelationship.sourceField` / `.targetField` | the line's ends, at the field rows, edge to edge. Cards whose columns overlap are joined on their right edges by a curve. An unknown field name anchors at the header, and the line tooltip names it. Both are required, so their probe moves the value between rows instead of unsetting it. | same |
| `DataModelRelationship.deleteBehavior` (new) | `on delete: VALUE` beside the label, and in the line tooltip | same |
| `ProcessDesignerSchema.version` | a badge beside the process name in the toolbar (`1.2` reads `v1.2`) | `ProcessDesigner.readers-11434.test.tsx` |
| `ProcessDesignerSchema.lanes` (`BPMNLane` `id` / `label` / `role` / `nodeIds`) | one band per lane around the nodes `nodeIds` names, labelled `LABEL · ROLE`, under the flows and nodes | same |
| `BPMNNode.assignee` / `.dueDate` | property-panel fields on a user task, and on any node that already carries a value | same |
| `BPMNNode.script` | a property-panel textarea on a script task, and on any node that carries one | same |
| `BPMNNode.properties` | one property-panel field per entry, under its key, with a control for the value's type. A non-primitive value is edited as JSON and committed once it parses. | same |
| `BPMNEdge.condition` | `[CONDITION]` on the flow, and in its tooltip | same |
| `BPMNEdge.isDefault` | BPMN's default-flow slash at the flow's source | same |

Supporting changes in the components:

- The entity card's header and rows now have constant heights (`h-9`, `h-6`), so the line anchors can be computed. The geometry constants restate those classes.
- Renaming a field on the canvas renames it in every relationship that names it on that entity, so its line stays on the row. This is pinned.
- `ProcessDesigner` destructures `version` and `lanes` now. It used to bind `lanes` to an unused name and never destructure `version`.
- `packages/plugin-designer/src/index.tsx` is untouched, so this PR does not overlap objectui#10859 phase 2b.

## The respelling: `onDelete` → `deleteBehavior`

- **Producers, measured first.** `git grep` over this repository found one producer, the `designer-zod-arms-10859` test fixture: 0 non-test and 1 test. ObjectStack has 0. The fixture now writes `deleteBehavior: 'cascade'`.
- **The new key.** `DataModelRelationship.deleteBehavior` is declared on both faces. The TS face reads its type off `@objectstack/spec`'s `Field['deleteBehavior']`, so the vocabulary cannot drift (`'set_null' | 'cascade' | 'restrict'`, pinned equal). The zod face restates the enum, and the mirror-parity rows compare the two.
- **The old key, refused by name on both faces.**
  - TS face: a `?: never` tombstone.
  - zod face: `aliasKeyRefusal`, which composes the spec's own lead sentence. Measured on `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0, `FieldSchema.safeParse` of a lookup field carrying `onDelete` answers `unrecognized_keys` with the named guidance "Did you mean `onDelete` → `deleteBehavior`?". So the spec refuses it as an unrecognized key and names the successor. The designer's refusal opens with the same sentence and then gives the migration. Before this PR, both designer faces accepted `onDelete`.
- **Migration line.** Rename the key to `deleteBehavior`. `cascade` and `restrict` keep their values, `set-null` becomes `set_null`, and `no-action` becomes `restrict` (the platform has no separate no-action; both refuse the delete while a reference remains). Every value it names is one the designer face can author.
- **Pin.** `designer-ondelete-respelled-11434.test.ts` holds the type rows (spec equality, both tombstones read `undefined`) and a `@ts-expect-error`. It also checks both runtime faces at path `relationships.0.onDelete`, the three new values accepted, and the two old literals refused under the new key. The render probe pins that `onDelete` reaches the component as a prop and draws nothing: no alias reads the old spelling.

- `UnmirroredDeclared`: **6 entries / 18 keys → 5 / 16**. The LOCAL half goes **3 / 4 → 2 / 2**: the `ProcessDesignerSchema` entry (`lanes`, `version`) leaves the ledger by REPAIR. Spec-derived stays 3 / 14.
- The union of the two unmirrored ledgers goes **11 → 10**. A history sentence is added at each pinned figure.
- `EXPECTED_MIRROR_PAIRS` goes **190 → 191**, for the new `designer.zod.ts#BPMNLaneSchema` pair. `BPMNLaneSchema` is exported from `@object-ui/types/zod`.

  - the `lanes` / `version` settlement row and the "arm omits" cases are replaced by an acceptance-and-refusal case for a lane;
  - the FULL fixture carries `version`, `lanes` and `deleteBehavior`.
- The objectui#7340 census goes **30 → 31**, with `designer.ts` going 1 → 2, for the `onDelete?: never` shape. `onDelete` joins the unambiguously retired names, because no live `onDelete` member remains in the types source. A history sentence is added.
- Pending changeset `10859-designer-zod-arms.md` gets a dated note. Its earlier note said `lanes` and `version` "are still unmirrored", and this PR makes that false.

## Changesets

- `@object-ui/types`: **minor**, with a **BREAKING (authoring)** banner for `onDelete`, `Clause-②: yes`, and the migration line.
- `@object-ui/plugin-designer`: **minor** (new drawn output; no prop changed).

## Size, for the split

The diff is 16 files, +1148 / −124:

- source: about 540 changed lines across the two components, `designer.ts`, `designer.zod.ts`, the barrel and the README;
- tests: about 600 lines;
- changesets: 53 lines.

That is in line with PR 1, and each designer's readers are self-contained, so the planned split stands.

## Reverse verification

- **Predicted, then run at BASE** (`c4ab6d09a` sources, this PR's tests; the five source files were swapped in under a restore trap):
  - Prediction: 27 red and 2 green. The two greens are the `onDelete`-draws-nothing pin and the runtime half of the `tsc` row.
  - Observed: **27 failed, 2 passed (29)**, exactly as predicted.
  - Type-level leg at BASE: `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` errors in the respelled pin's assertion rows, its `@ts-expect-error` and its `deleteBehavior` literal, in the arms test's `BPMNLane` import and the lane and `process-designer` key-set rows, and in the parity file's import and ledger assertions.
- **Ablation A** (`anchorY` ignores the field name):
  - Predicted 4 red; observed **6 red**.
  - The prediction missed that the target end also falls to the header, which reddens the unknown-name row. It also missed that both "has no field" notes then enter the tooltip, which reddens the exact-title assertion of the `deleteBehavior` row.
- **Ablation B** (the `properties.` prefix stops routing into the record): predicted 2 red; observed **2 red**, the two edit rows.
- **Landing and restore proofs.**
  - Each mutation went through `ablation-replace.mjs`: anchor 1 → 0, replacement 0 → 1, blob moved, and an independent `grep -c` of both strings.
  - Each restore was by `git checkout HEAD --`, proven by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`. A trap repeated the restore for the BASE leg.
